correctness.rationale: A primitive period-two flip at an internal degree-two site forces both neighbors to flip in alternating opposite phase, propagating along an entire path to both terminals. The degree-three terminal majorities require two active paths or one active path with opposing fixed-path terminal bits at each terminal. Every stationary path of length at least three is exactly a binary word with all runs of size at least two; length two has a separate opposite-terminal tie condition. The complete and disjoint support classification derives the formula with phase division checked. Generating functions and Fibonacci-six-periodic equal-arm asymptotics are algebraically derived. Full-state brute-force and independent constructive verifiers were replayed from the packaged standalone sources, with reproducible exact outputs; finite tests are not offered as universal proof.

value.rationale: Three-path theta graphs are the minimal 2-connected two-cycle family with two branching terminals. The all-parameter exact orbit and oscillating-support classification resolves a natural dynamical invariant, while the surprising one-channel dominance is explained by opposite static boundary support. The equal-arm quadratic-Fibonacci versus linear-Fibonacci scale separation is structural and mathematically motivated; the result is not a routine parameter increment.
